title: They rebuilt the Fish Gate… but nobody talks about what it smelled like.
paragraphs: They rebuilt the Fish Gate… but nobody talks about what it smelled like.
Rot.
Salt.
Commerce.
Life and decay colliding at one entrance.
In Nehemiah 3:3, the Fish Gate goes up again—hands working, stones rising, purpose returning. But this wasn’t a pretty gate. This was where fishermen entered. Where the city’s appetite was fed.
Messy.
Noisy.
Necessary.
And here’s what we miss…
God didn’t start the restoration with the palace.
He rebuilt the places that smelled like survival.
Because before glory, there is grit.
Before worship rises, something broken must be repaired.
But shift the lens.
In Zephaniah 1:10, a cry echoes from that same gate.
Judgment.
The very place of provision becomes a place of warning.
Why?
Because what feeds you can also rule you.
What sustains you can slowly replace God.
And that’s where grace walks in.
Jesus Christ stood by another shoreline… calling fishermen.
“Follow Me.”
Not to build gates.
But to become fishers of men.
He didn’t reject the smell of their world.
He redeemed it.
Listen, kapatid.
Your “Fish Gate” might be the part of your life that feels messy… transactional… survival-driven.
Your hustle.
Your hidden habits.
Your quiet compromises.
God is not afraid to step there.
But He refuses to leave it unchanged.
Rebuild it.
Surrender it.
Let Jesus redefine what enters your life—and what flows out of it.
Because the same place that once fed your flesh…
can become the place where God feeds your calling.
